invariants.rotationUnitPowerOfTwo: The band's ROTATION UNIT in bytes must be a power of two — rows * TILE_BYTES on a horizontal band, cols * TILE_BYTES on a vertical one (aeon `band_axis_geometry`: `unit_bytes = a[_AXIS_UNIT_TILES[axis]] * 32`, `unit_shift = unit_bytes.bit_length() - 1`, `assert (1 << unit_shift) == unit_bytes`). The rule keeps its SHAPE across the axes — the runtime rotates a whole unit by SHIFTING — and changes only which band key it is spelled on. Was `columnBytesPowerOfTwo`, which stated the horizontal reading as if it were the only one.
invariants.patternPeriod: pattern_px == the period ALONG THE AXIS: cols * TILE_WIDTH_PX on a horizontal band, rows * TILE_WIDTH_PX on a vertical one (aeon `band_axis_geometry` returns `period_tiles * 8`; `main()` asserts `pattern_px == period_px`). Was `patternWidth`, which is the horizontal name for it.
invariants.contiguousPacking: bands pack contiguously from slot 0 in list order; slot_base, when present, must equal the running cursor
invariants.insideTheBlob: slot_base + cols*rows <= len(tiles) for every band
invariants.prefixIdentity: phases[0] == tiles[slot_base : slot_base + cols*rows] — the band's rest state IS the static tiles it covers. This is the invariant that makes anims/tiles/layout ONE unit rather than three separable keys: a violation bakes CLEANLY and ships silently corrupt art, and every other assert in the consumer still passes (aeon docs/BUGS.md TOOL-01; tools/bg_override_io.py's docstring; aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCoherence).
invariants.capacity: len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY. Animated slots are a PREFIX of tiles, NOT an addition — they cost no capacity beyond the array that already holds them (empyrean §5.1, which corrects an earlier `tiles + animated slots <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY` rule that would have told Aurora the flagship act cannot carry any band at all). THE CEILING IS A DECLARED ALLOCATION AND IT HAS ALREADY MOVED ONCE (448 -> 400 at aeon EFFECTS-W1 item 9d, when 48 slots were reassigned to `waterline_strips`). Never restate the number in prose or a test: read `constants.BG_TILE_CAPACITY.value`, which is what every consumer in this repo does.
invariants.layoutTileIndex: layout[row*64 + col] is a nametable word whose low LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK bits are a blob-local index into `tiles` and whose remaining bits are attributes the consumer preserves — EXCEPT that a word of exactly 0 is passed through unrebased and renders VRAM tile 0 (blank) rather than tiles[0]. Adding or removing a band renumbers `tiles`, so every nonzero word must be rewritten INDEX-ONLY, and a rewrite that would produce the value 0 is unrepresentable rather than merely different.
invariants.slotOrder: WRITER OBLIGATION 1, and the consumer CANNOT CHECK IT. Band cell (c, r) is slot `slot_base + c*rows + r` on a HORIZONTAL band (column-major) and `slot_base + r*cols + c` on a VERTICAL one (ROW-major). It lives in `layout` — which cell references which slot — and the same set of slots reads as a scroll under one order and as a shimmer under the other. aeon: 'a band's slots are deduped against the static blob and appear at many cells — so nothing checks this'. Any Aurora assertion over the SET, the COUNT or a CHECKSUM of a band's slots is vacuous here by construction; only the ORDER discriminates.
invariants.phaseAxis: WRITER OBLIGATION 2. The eight phase banks must be translations ALONG THE DECLARED AXIS. aeon refuses exactly one case and admits everything else: a vertical band whose phases are exact HORIZONTAL translations of phase 0 and are not also vertical ones (`validate_band_phase_axis`) — the reachable accident of a horizontal-only shift-fill run over a band declared vertical. Composites are deliberately admitted on both axes, because the shipped horizontal bands are composites rather than pure rolls.
invariants.sectionCeiling: THE SECOND BUDGET, AND THE TIGHTER ONE ON EVERY DOCUMENT MEASURED SO FAR. `BGANIM_COUNT_BYTES + BGANIM_RECORD_BYTES*bands + views*(BGANIM_COUNT_BYTES + BGANIM_RECORD_BYTES*bands) + total_animated_slots*BGANIM_BYTES_PER_SLOT <= BGANIM_SECTION_CEILING` (aeon `bganim_section_bytes` and `check_bganim_section_fits`). IT IS ON THE ACT'S TOTAL AND NEVER PER BAND: `BgAnim_Banks` is one blob for the whole act, and aeon's own comment records a per-band cap being tried and refuted by this zone's shipped content (32x4 + 16x4 passes any generous per-band limit while its SUM is 49,242 B). `views` is BGANIM_VIEW_COUNT or zero and is decided PER ACT, not per band — see `viewTwins`. ⚠ IT IS INDEPENDENT OF `capacity`: a document can sit far inside BG_TILE_CAPACITY and be refused here, which is exactly the state aeon's live document was in when this was found. NEVER RESTATE EITHER NUMBER: derive both and say which one binds.
invariants.viewTwins: HOW MANY DEBUG VIEW TWINS AN ACT EMITS, and therefore an operand of `sectionCeiling`. Zero unless some band carries `default_off`; otherwise BGANIM_VIEW_COUNT, and only if the act has EXACTLY ONE BAND whose `pattern_px` is BGANIM_VIEW_DERIVED_PERIOD_PX — aeon raises on either failure rather than emitting zero twins. ⚠ BOTH REFUSALS ARE QUANTIFIED OVER THE ACT, NOT OVER THE BANDS THAT CARRY THE KEY: a two-band act in which BOTH bands are `default_off` is refused just as a mixed one is, so a validator asking 'do the bands agree?' passes a document this build rejects. See `bandKeys.default_off.writerObligations`.
invariants.axisRoundTrip: WRITER OBLIGATION 3. `axis` must survive a load / edit-something-else / save. Dropping it silently reverts the band to horizontal, and obligation 2's guard cannot see a band that no longer claims to be vertical. Absent means "horizontal", and Aurora never writes the default in — a save of an untouched document is not a diff.

amendments.lesson: A FIGURE WITH NO CAUSE AND NO END CONDITION CANNOT AGE, SO IT IS ALWAYS READ AS SETTLED. This file has now been wrong about this one number three times — 448, then 400, and it would have been 388 if anyone had re-vendored eight hours earlier — and each previous entry recorded the new value as though the movement were over. The movement is not a plan anyone is holding: aeon's object tile neighbourhood is fully spent, one free tile in the whole 2048-tile map, so this arena's unresident reserve is the cheapest address space on the machine and the next object needing tiles will reach for it exactly as the spring did twice. It ends at aeon's deliberate VRAM re-cut, booked and waiting on the owner's word. That is why `constants.BG_TILE_CAPACITY.why` now states the PROPERTY and the end condition instead of narrating the latest hop. AND THE SECOND HALF, WHICH IS AEON'S: the addresses a parcel MOVES are a different population from the addresses it TOUCHES, and only the second is reachable by grepping your own diff — both spring parcels moved this ceiling and neither opened the file whose comment restated it. The sweep that follows a value change must therefore be over every place that RESTATES the value, not over the files the change edited; and where prose can name the authority symbol and let the constant answer, DELETE the literal rather than re-typing today's, because a fresh number goes stale on the identical clock.
